speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've described significant symptoms like fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin narrowing this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detail. Have you noticed any fever, itching (pruritus), or changes in your appetite? Also, has there been any blood in your stool or difficulty swallowing?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, ESR, and CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal; Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated; ESR: Normal Readings; CRP: Normal Readings. Imaging: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy: Cervical Lymph Node findings indicate Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal Examination: Slight abdominal distension, normal bowel sounds, dullness noted over the left lower quadrant, splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma with gastrointestinal involvement).
